subject: Canary deadman fired (eu) — request to pin traffic / temporary rollback for model v10.2
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:12:00Z
Subject: [Alert] Canary deadman fired — model v10.2 (eu-west-1) P95 latency > 2s

Hi team,

Canary for model v10.2 in eu-west-1 tripped the deadman rule at 08:07 UTC. P95 spiked to ~2.4s over the last 10m (baseline ~0.9s). The canary pool is small (5% traffic), but error rates are stable; this looks like a latency regression rather than availability. Attached: canary_stats_20260929.csv and a quick p95 trend screenshot.

Initial observations:
- Increased self-hosted kernel jitter correlating with sequence lengths > 512 tokens.
- Affected % of requests concentrated on a single shard (shard-7).

Immediate ask: advise if we should pin Apollo Health traffic to v10.1 (previous stable) and initiate a staged rollback/canary revert. SLA note: Apollo is on a 99.9% p95 commitment in EU; this may trigger an exception.

I recommend:
1) Pin Apollo (DEAL-2247) to v10.1 for 1h while infra triages.
2) Open a mitigation ticket with runtime team to isolate shard-7.
3) Notify customer and surface compensation options if needed.

I can push a traffic pin within 15m once we have approval.

-Markus
Lead SRE
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@apollohealth.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:22:00Z
Subject: Re: [Alert] Canary deadman fired — model v10.2 (eu-west-1) P95 latency > 2s

Carlos / Apollo team —

Thanks for the rapid heads up, Markus. Carlos, we see a short-lived P95 spike in the canary for the v10.2 rollout. We want to be proactive: we plan to pin Apollo traffic back to v10.1 for a short window while we assess the regression.

Proposed immediate plan (needs your OK):
- Pin Apollo traffic to v10.1 for an initial 1 hour (can extend if needed).
- Do a staged canary rollback on our side; monitor p95 and error rate for 30m post-pin.
- If we confirm regression on v10.2, we will keep Apollo on v10.1 until v10.2 patch is validated.

If you approve, Ben will coordinate the customer-facing times and any credit/SLAs. Karthik, can product sign off on a 1-hour pin as a safety measure? Naomi, echoing for CS to track communication.

Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@apollohealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Canary deadman — proposed rollback/pin for Apollo Health (DEAL-2247)

Carlos — quick note from the commercial side. We recommend the short pin to v10.1 to avoid user impact while SRE investigates. We can offer the following to address SLA exposure:
- Temporary SLA carveout for the affected 1h window (we will log the incident and provide a follow-up postmortem).
- If p95 breach extends beyond 4 hours, we will discuss a pro-rated credit per the contract.

I’ve attached a one-page mutual action plan (mutual_action_plan_APOLLO-2247.pdf) with the rollback steps and expected timelines. If you reply OK, we will schedule the pin for immediate execution and inform you when it’s complete.

- Ben
Account Executive
From: Carlos Mendez <carlos.m@apollohealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, SRE Team <sre@apollohealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Canary deadman — proposed rollback/pin for Apollo Health (DEAL-2247)

Ben / Marissa —

OK to proceed with the 1h pin to v10.1 immediately. Please confirm the start/end times and the exact behavioral check you will use to unpin. We are running time-sensitive workflows between 09:30 and 10:30 UTC, so please avoid the bulk of our high-throughput window if possible.

Also, we need the carveout window documented for our compliance team — can you provide a short email we can route internally stating the reason and duration? Attached is a screenshot from our end showing elevated p95 on our traffic.

Thanks,
Carlos
CTO, Apollo Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T12:45:00Z
Subject: Actioned: Traffic pinned + scheduled revert checks — summary for SLA record

Team —

Per approvals, I executed the traffic pin at 09:12 UTC (Apollo traffic moved to v10.1). We monitored for 60 minutes; P95 for Apollo returned to baseline (~0.95s) within 18 minutes post-pin. No errors or falls in throughput observed.

Notes for record and for Carlos’ compliance team:
- Action: Pin Apollo Health (DEAL-2247) traffic from v10.2 -> v10.1.
- Start: 2026-09-29T09:12:00Z
- End: 2026-09-29T10:12:00Z (pin released after confirmation of stability)
- Reason: Canary deadman triggered due to P95 latency regression traced to shard-7 on v10.2.
- Follow-ups: Runtime team to run kernel/regression fix; postmortem scheduled and will include root cause and remediation ETA.

I’ve logged the incident and attached the p95 trend PNG and the mutual action plan to the HubSpot ticket (link above). Ben — please confirm commercial note for the carveout and any customer credit. Karthik / Markus — please prioritize the runtime investigation.

Naomi
Customer Solutions Manager
